title: States
description: States show the interaction status of a component or UI element

contentChunks.htmlValue:
• States have two visual indicators to ensure accessibility
  • States can be combined, such as selection and hover
  • Apply states consistently across components

contentChunks.htmlValue: State layers

A state layer is a semi-transparent covering on an element that indicates its state. State layers provide a systematic approach to visualizing states by using opacity. A layer can be applied to an entire element or in a circular shape and only one state layer can be applied at a given time.

To transition from an enabled style to a stateful style requires the addition of a state layer.

The state layer is an overlay with a fixed opacity for each state and uses the same color as the content. 

For example, if the enabled style uses the secondary container color for the container and on secondary container for content, the state layer will be an overlay using the on secondary container color.  

If the enabled style uses the surface color for the container and the primary color role for content, then the state layer will be an overlay using the primary color.

contentChunks.footer:
1. Container
  2. State layer
  3. Content
contentChunks.altText: State layer sandwiched between the container and content.

contentChunks.htmlValue: The size of state layers is 40dp while the interactive target size is 48dp.

contentChunks.footer:

contentChunks.htmlValue:
On colors

By default, a component’s state layer color is derived from the color of its content, either the color of an icon or label text if no icon is present.

An on color is a color role used by the content. Each container color has its own corresponding on color. 

For example, if a container color is secondary container, the content will use the on secondary container color role.

contentChunks.footer: Order of surface layers shows the state layer (2) between the container (1) and content (3) layers
contentChunks.altText: State layer sandwiched between  the content and container.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
State layer tokens & values

The state layer uses a fixed percentage for the opacity for each state. A state layer uses the color used by content (usually the on color) and the percentage opacity for its respective state.

contentChunks.footer:
Four overlay states and their values:

  1. Hover +8% opacity 
  2. Focus +10% opacity 
  3. Press +10% opacity
  4. Drag +16% opacity
contentChunks.altText: The opacity values of four overlay states.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Activated states

Unlike hover, focus, pressed, and dragged states that use state layers, the container and content of activated components change color directly. 

Activated components use the secondary container color for the component container and change the content color to on secondary container.

contentChunks.footer: Activated state
contentChunks.altText: Activated flights container with color changed compared to containers for hotels, and restaurants both not in activated state.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Enabled
An enabled state communicates an interactive component or element. Enabled states use the default styling for each interactive component.

contentChunks.footer:
Enabled states for:

  1. Button
  2. FAB
  3. Switch
  4. Text field
contentChunks.altText: Enabled state of 4 components.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Disabled

A disabled state communicates when a component or element isn’t interactive. This state is visually communicated through color changes and reduced elevation.

Disabled states don't need to meet Material's contrast requirements.

contentChunks.footer: Disabled button
contentChunks.altText: Low opacity solitary button labeled disabled, indicates a  disabled/inoperable state.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Disabled states are inherited by action, selection, and input components:

  • Buttons
  • Cards
  • Checkboxes
  • Chips
  • List items
  • Radio buttons
  • Switches
  • Text fields

contentChunks.footer:
Disabled states for:

  1. Checkbox
  2. Icon button
  3. Radio button
  4. Segmented button
contentChunks.altText: Inoperable state of 4 components.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Disabled states aren't inherited by communication, containment, navigation, and some actions components: 

  • App bars
  • Badges
  • Dialogs
  • Floating action buttons (FABs)
  • Menus
  • Navigation bar, drawer, and rail
  • Sheets
  • Tabs
  • Tooltips

contentChunks.footer: If the action represented in the FAB is unavailable, the FAB shouldn't appear
contentChunks.altText: Screen erroneously showing edit FAB in inoperable state, though the edit function is unavailable.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Behavior

Disabled components can’t be focused, dragged, or pressed, and they don’t change state when tapped or hovered over.

contentChunks.footer: A disabled button doesn’t inherit hover or other state layers
contentChunks.altText: A cursor moves over and clicks on an disabled/inoperable button and the button doesn’t change.

contentChunks.htmlValue: There can be any number of disabled states in a layout.

contentChunks.footer:
1. Disabled redo icon button
  2. Disabled checklist icon button
contentChunks.altText: Disabled components on a screen.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Hover

Hover states are initiated by the user pausing over an interactive element using a cursor.

The lower-emphasis surface overlay for hover states can be applied to the entire component, elements within a component, or as a circular shape over part of the component.

contentChunks.footer: Hovered button
contentChunks.altText: Cursor moves toward button which reads “enabled” and when the cursor touches the button text changes to “hovered.”

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Hover states are inherited by action, selection, and input components:

  • Buttons
  • Cards
  • Checkbox
  • Chips
  • Date and time pickers
  • List items
  • Slider
  • Switch
  • Text fields

contentChunks.footer:
Hovered states for:

  1. FAB
  2. Icon button
  3. Chip
  4. Segmented buttons
contentChunks.altText: Hover state of 4 components.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Hover states aren’t inherited by communication, containment, or navigation components: 

  • App bars
  • Badges
  • Dialogs
  • Menus
  • Navigation bar, drawer, and rail
  • Sheets
  • Tabs

contentChunks.footer: The individual components that are actionable within the app bar inherit hover states, not the whole app bar

contentChunks.htmlValue: Focused

A focused state communicates when a user has highlighted an element using a keyboard or voice. Focus states apply to all interactive components.

The higher-emphasis surface overlay for focused states can be applied to the entire component, elements within a component, or as a circular shape over part of the component.

contentChunks.footer: Focused button
contentChunks.altText: A button in focused state.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Focus states are inherited by action, selection, and input components:

  • Buttons
  • Cards
  • Checkbox
  • Chips
  • Date and time pickers
  • List items
  • Selection controls
  • Text fields

contentChunks.footer:
Focused states for:

  1. FAB
  2. Icon button
  3. Chip
  4. Segmented buttons
contentChunks.altText: Focus state of 4 components.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Focus states aren’t inherited by most communication, containment, or navigation components:

  • App bars
  • Badges
  • Banner
  • Card
  • Dialogs
  • Navigation bar, drawer, and rail
  • Sheets

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Keyboard focus indicator

Many people use the Tab key or other shortcut to navigate the interactive elements of a web page, like links, buttons, and chips.

When an element is tabbed to, it appears in its focused state with a ring-like keyboard focus indicator. This indicator helps web users know where they are on the page.

While focused, an element can be acted on with the keyboard.

contentChunks.footer: Keyboard focus indicator for a filled button
contentChunks.altText: A single filled button in focused state, displaying the keyboard focus indicator.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Behavior

Focus states are initiated by the user by pressing the Tab key on the keyboard (or equivalent).

Focus states can be represented in combination with hover, activated, or selected states.

contentChunks.footer: A selected filter chip in both selected and focused states
contentChunks.altText: A single filter chip simultaneously in selected state and focus state.

contentChunks.htmlValue: There can only be one focus state at a time in a layout.

contentChunks.footer: A focus state applied to one card at a time
contentChunks.altText: Cursor moving from one card in focus state to another card moves the focus state to the second card.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Activated

Activated states indicate which item from a set of options is currently being viewed. They are initiated either by default or user choice, using input methods such as a tap, cursor, keyboard, or voice input. 

Activated states are higher emphasis and signified by an overlay, color change, or other visual treatments applied to elements or segments within a component.

contentChunks.footer: Activated tab
contentChunks.altText: The activated tab has a different color and shape than the enabled tabs.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
An activated state differs from a selected state because it communicates a highlighted destination.

Activation states are inherited by items within some navigation components: 

✓ Navigation bar, drawer, and rail
✓ Tabs

contentChunks.footer: Tab (1) and navigation drawer (2) with activated states
contentChunks.altText: The tab and navigation drawer are both in activated states.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Activation states aren’t inherited by action, communication, containment, selection, or input components: 

✗ App bars
✗ Badges
✗ Buttons
✗ Checkbox
✗ Chips
✗ Dialogs
✗ Sheets
✗ Sliders
✗ Switch
✗ Text fields

contentChunks.footer: Activated states are applied to navigational components, like tab items, to indicate a destination, not action components, like a button
contentChunks.altText: Activated state applied to a button in error.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Behavior

Activated states can be represented in combination with hover and focus states.

contentChunks.footer: Activated states appear in user-initiated order
contentChunks.altText: A cursor hovers over unselected button in a hovered state.  On a click it switches to active state.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Activated states can be represented in combination with hover and focus states.

contentChunks.altText: Screen showing inbox in focus and activated states.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Within a single set of options, only one activated state may be present at a time.

contentChunks.altText: Email settings navigation list “inbox”is activated. The selection components has one activated state as well.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Pressed

A pressed state communicates a user-initiated tap or click via cursor, keyboard, or voice input. This state applies to all interactive components.

Pressed states trigger a change in composition and should be high-emphasis.

A ripple overlay signifies a pressed state. It can be applied to an entire component or elements within a component, or as a circular shape over part of the component.

contentChunks.footer: Pressed button
contentChunks.altText: Button using a ripple overlay to signify it’s in a pressed state.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Some components, such as buttons or cards, can inherit elevation to signify a pressed state.

contentChunks.footer: Pressed button with elevation
contentChunks.altText: Button using elevation to signify it’s in a pressed state.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Pressed states are inherited by action, selection, and some containment components: 

  • Buttons
  • Cards
  • Checkbox
  • Chips
  • List items
  • Text fields

contentChunks.footer:
Pressed states for:

  1. FAB
  2. Icon button
  3. Chip

contentChunks.altText: Four components shown in pressed state.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Pressed states aren’t inherited by communication, navigation, or some containment components: 

  • App bars

  • Menus
  • Sheets
  • Tabs

contentChunks.footer: The individual components that are actionable within the app bar inherit pressed states, not the whole app bar

Pressed states are initiated by user keyboard or voice input on an interactive element.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Dragged

A dragged state occurs when a user presses and moves an element or component. Dragged states should be low emphasis, to avoid distracting users from their task.

Dragged states use a lower emphasis overlay. It can be applied to the entire component or to elements within a component.

Some components, such as list items, chips, or cards, can inherit elevation to signify a dragged state.

contentChunks.footer: Dragged list item
contentChunks.altText: List item shown in dragged state.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Dragged states are inherited by some containment and selection components: 

  • Cards
  • Chips
  • List items
  • Sliders

contentChunks.footer:
Dragged states for:

  1. Chip
  2. Card
contentChunks.altText: A chip and a card both shown in dragged state.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Dragged states aren’t inherited by action, communication, navigation, or some containment components: 

  • App bars
  • Badges
  • Buttons
  • Dialogs
  • Menus
  • Navigation bar, drawer, and rail

contentChunks.footer: Components like an app bar that require consistent placement should not inherit dragged states
contentChunks.altText: Mobile screen with app bar in dragged state is an error.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Behavior

Dragged states are initiated when users touch and hold elements, using an input method such as a tap or click.

contentChunks.altText: Going through the states of a draggable list item:  enabled, hovered, dragged.

contentChunks.htmlValue: There may only be a single dragged state at a time within a layout.
